clue.text: Poor work disrupting railway

indicators.note: to disrupt a line is to break into it, so one piece is pushed inside the other

blocks.note: RY is the standard abbreviation for railway
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Shoddy engineering works are causing delays on the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: ROPY is informal British for poor or shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally in Britain, something ropy is of inferior quality, shabby or in bad condition.

clue.text: Wine picked up in can is terrible

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the words that follow
in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters straddling can, is and the start of terrible

explanation.surface: Someone tasting wine from a can declares it awful.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'can is terrible' backwards and RETSINA appears across can, is and terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Wandering from pier, awfully sad, missing hotel

indicators.note: done awfully, the word is botched and its letters come out in a poor order
something missing is absent, so a letter must be dropped

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
pathetic means pitiful or sad
H is Hotel in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone drifts sadly away from the seaside pier and away from the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles only pier; sad is a straight synonym, and hotel is the letter it must lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Peripatetic describes someone travelling from place to place, roaming about rather than staying settled.

clue.text: Insult hero's unusually soft style of singing

indicators.note: arranged unusually, the letters appear out of their normal order

blocks.note: a barb is a cutting remark
the five letters rearranged
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: An insult directed at a hero comes across as oddly gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in hero's is ignored, leaving five letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbershop is close-harmony unaccompanied singing, typically by a male quartet, so it names a vocal genre.

clue.text: Assistance guarding against becoming zealous

indicators.note: to guard something is to keep it surrounded and protected

blocks.note: aid is help
V is versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: Helping to protect against something makes a person passionate about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid and zealous are synonyms, both meaning keenly enthusiastic and eager about a pursuit.

clue.text: Recoil in anger, struggling after prosperous period

indicators.note: a word that is struggling is in disarray, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a boom is a time of economic growth
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: After a period of prosperity, people react with angry recoil as things fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the period first in the answer even though it comes last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, boomerang means to rebound or backfire on the originator, like the curved throwing stick coming back.

clue.text: Remembrance mostly about one with dream showing obstinacy

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter goes

blocks.note: recall is the act of remembering
C is circa, Latin for about
I is the Roman numeral one
a trance is a dreamlike state

explanation.surface: Remembering a dream proves stubbornly difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here is not a reversal or container signal but the abbreviation C, circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalcitrance is a stubborn refusal to obey or cooperate, the same quality as obstinacy.

clue.text: Fish not caught in centre of activity

indicators.note: not having a letter means it is taken away

blocks.note: the chub is a freshwater fish
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An angler's fish escapes, right in the middle of the action.
explanation.walkthrough: On a cricket scorecard 'c' records a batter out caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A hub is the central point of a network or operation where most of the activity happens.

clue.text: Refinement in language

blocks.note: first meaning: elegance or finesse
second meaning: the tongue spoken in Poland

explanation.surface: Elegance shown in the way someone speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter is hidden at the start of the clue: refinement is lower-case polish, the language upper-case Polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish means sophistication and finish, and also names the Slavic tongue spoken by people of Poland.

clue.text: Director getting Oscar, after cheers, blustering endlessly

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thanks
ranting is loud, blustering speech
O is Oscar in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A film director wins an Oscar, then gives a rambling acceptance speech after the applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after cheers' places the piece for cheers first; in Britain 'cheers' and 'ta' both mean thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is an American film-maker known for Pulp Fiction, an example of a director.

clue.text: One man ends all wrangling as leader of South Africa

indicators.note: wrangling is quarrelling and tangling, so the preceding letters get mixed up

blocks.note: every letter of these four words is used

explanation.surface: A single man brings an end to all the arguing and becomes the nation's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is close to an and-lit: Mandela was indeed one man who ended a long struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first black president in 1994, after ending apartheid through negotiation.

clue.text: Labour account about conspiratorial group

indicators.note: brought about, the pair turns round and reads the other way

blocks.note: Lab is the short form of the UK Labour Party
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A tale of a plotting faction inside the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' applies to both abbreviations together, not just to account.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabal is a secret faction of plotters working together, especially in politics.

clue.text: Stick with demon drink

blocks.note: an imp is a small demon
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Keeping company with a devilish drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce or skewer something with a pointed object, a verb sense of stick.

clue.text: Pragmatic people referring to ace catalogues

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
A is ace on playing cards
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: Practical types like to point to their excellent inventories.
explanation.definitionFit: Realists accept situations as they actually are and deal with them practically, which is what pragmatists do.

clue.text: Oddity in wrong version of a liturgy

indicators.note: a different version presents the same letters in another form

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Something odd crops up in a corrupted form of church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' looks like part of the anagram signal, but it is a noun giving its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A singularity is a peculiarity or strange trait, something odd that marks a thing out.

clue.text: Deeds unfamiliar to saint in order to prepare for battle

indicators.note: made unfamiliar, the words appear in a strange, unrecognisable order

blocks.note: actions are deeds
these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Actions a saint would not recognise, done to get ready for war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' looks like an anagram signal, but it belongs to the link 'in order to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Action stations is the military order for crew to take up positions ready for combat, a call to get set for fighting.

clue.text: Ruined contest, losing force and clinging

indicators.note: what is lost is no longer there, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: skint is British slang for penniless
a fight is a contest
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A bankrupt boxer drops out of a bout, still hanging on.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is everyday British slang for broke, so 'ruined' in its financial sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Skintight clothing fits closely against the body, hugging it the way something clinging does.

clue.text: Territory shown by map sadly secured by fraud and crushed

indicators.note: done sadly, the word is spoiled and its letters fall out of order
something secured by another is held fast inside it

blocks.note: a sting is a confidence trick
the three letters rearranged
ground is crushed into powder

explanation.surface: Land on a map, sadly taken by deception and flattened.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamping ground is a place a person habitually frequents, their familiar patch or haunt.

clue.text: Teacher keeping record on Hawaii identifying marine mammal

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within

blocks.note: a don is a university teacher
an LP is a long-playing record
HI is the postal abbreviation for Hawaii

explanation.surface: A teacher with a record of time in Hawaii can recognise sea creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the record before Hawaii, and the pair sits inside the teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolphins are aquatic, air-breathing cetaceans living in the sea, so they fit as an ocean mammal.

clue.text: Investigator with eggs upset bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: tec is slang for detective
ova is Latin for eggs

explanation.surface: A detective knocks over a nest of eggs, upsetting the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal, but in a down clue it flips the whole thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill, emblem of the RSPB.

clue.text: Neighbourhood very hostile about fashionable appeal

indicators.note: about means around, so one part goes round the others

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
an icy welcome is hostile
in means trendy
it is sex appeal

explanation.surface: A local area strongly hostile to anything trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal comes from 1920s slang, as in the It girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The vicinity is the area near or surrounding a place, its neighbourhood.

clue.text: Call for extremes of exertion before end

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters
the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: A demand for maximum effort right up to the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to require or necessitate it, so a plan may demand that consequence.

clue.text: Bishop during meal raised support

indicators.note: something happening during an event is inside its span
in a down clue, raising the letters makes them read from bottom to top

blocks.note: tea is an evening meal in Britain
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop raises support during a church supper.
explanation.walkthrough: In much of Britain tea is the evening meal, not just a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, usually in wrongdoing, which is a form of support.

clue.text: Heart broken by hard task

indicators.note: a thing broken into has something forced inside it

blocks.note: the core is the heart of something
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A demanding job leaves someone heartbroken.
explanation.definitionFit: A chore is a routine, often tedious job, especially domestic work around the house.

clue.text: Sash used by slob incorrectly

indicators.note: the letters are borrowed from within the words that follow

blocks.note: runs across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A lazy person wears a sash the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' tempts as an anagram signal, but the answer sits in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash worn around the waist with a Japanese kimono.

clue.text: Sigh woefully about bribe, confounded nonsense

indicators.note: done woefully, the word is badly made and its letters disordered
about means around, so one set of letters surrounds the other
confounded means thrown into confusion, so these letters are mixed too

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sighs miserably over a bribe, muttering confused nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are scrambled, so treating all nine letters as one anagram also works.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibberish is unintelligible talk or meaningless language, the same thing as nonsense.

clue.text: Dance with skill, I note, having three elements

blocks.note: to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic
art is skill
taken as written
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A dancer remarks that the routine combines three components.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripartite means consisting of or divided into three parts, as in a three-party agreement.

clue.text: Contents of rhyme and new song

indicators.note: the contents of a word are what lies inside, without its outer letters

blocks.note: the inner letters
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: The words of a fresh rhyme set to music.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song of praise sung in church, so it is a kind of song.
